questions.def: 'Were' + to-infinitive expresses a formal hypothetical condition.
questions.question: Were he to decline the offer, what ___ the alternative?

questions.def: 'Had' + past participle implies a past unreal condition.
questions.question: Had I known the truth, I ___ differently.

questions.def: Perfect participle indicates a prior action and its consequence.
questions.question: ___ the implications, he would have hesitated.

questions.def: 'Supposing' introduces a formal hypothetical with subjunctive 'were'.
questions.question: Supposing that ___ to win, what would he do?

questions.def: Inverted conditional 'were it not' needs 'would have' in result clause.
questions.question: Were it not for his assistance, we ___ failed.

questions.def: 'Had' requires the past participle to form the past unreal conditional.
questions.question: Had I ___, I would have acted differently.

questions.def: 'But for' introduces an exception to a hypothetical situation.
questions.question: But ___ that he intervened, the situation would have escalated.

questions.def: 'Only if' requires subject-verb inversion and indicates a condition.
questions.question: Only if the evidence ___ conclusive, will action be taken.

questions.def: 'Granting' introduces a conditional assumption in a formal style.
questions.question: ___ that the premise is true, the conclusion follows.

questions.def: 'Lest' is followed by the subjunctive 'be' to express avoidance.
questions.question: Lest he ___ perceived as biased, he recused himself.

questions.def: 'In the event that' requires present simple for future condition.
questions.question: In the event that the proposal ___ rejected, we will reconsider.

questions.def: 'Assuming' introduces a conditional clause and a premise.
questions.question: ___ that the data is accurate, the results are valid.

questions.def: 'Only through' emphasizes the necessity of hard work.
questions.question: Only ___ hard work will achieve success.

questions.def: 'Not until' requires subject-verb inversion and a condition.
questions.question: Not until the report ___ submitted will the decision be made.

questions.def: 'Provided' introduces a conditional clause.
questions.question: ___ that all criteria are met, the application will proceed.

questions.def: 'Given these' introduces the context for the conclusion.
questions.question: Given ___ circumstances, the outcome was predictable.

questions.def: 'Scarcely had' requires subject-verb inversion and a past action.
questions.question: Scarcely ___ he entered the room when the phone rang.

questions.def: 'Considering' introduces the evidence for the conclusion.
questions.question: ___ the evidence, a different conclusion emerges.

questions.def: 'On condition that' introduces a necessary condition.
questions.question: On condition ___ the agreement is signed, the project will commence.

questions.def: 'Seldom' requires subject-verb inversion in formal writing.
questions.question: Seldom ___ such dedication to public service.

questions.def: 'Permitting' creates a conditional participial phrase.
questions.question: ___ circumstances permitting, we shall proceed as planned.

questions.def: Inverted third conditional: "Had it not been for..." replaces "If it had not been for...".
questions.question: ___ it not been for your help, I would have failed.

questions.def: 'No sooner was' requires subject-verb inversion and a past action.
questions.question: No sooner ___ the announcement made than chaos erupted.

questions.def: 'Were' + to-infinitive expresses a hypothetical situation in formal conditionals.
questions.question: Were he to decline, what ___ the next course of action?

questions.def: 'Had' + past participle introduces a past unreal conditional clause.
questions.question: Had I known, I ___ differently.

questions.def: Perfect participle expresses a reason for a past action.
questions.question: ___ the full implications, the committee hesitated.

questions.def: 'Only then' requires subject-verb inversion for emphasis.
questions.question: Only then ___ the full extent of the damage.

questions.def: 'Such...that' introduces a result clause, showing consequence.
questions.question: Such was his determination ___ he refused to give up.

questions.def: 'Granted' introduces a conditional clause, meaning 'If I were granted'.
questions.question: ___ the opportunity, I would accept immediately.

questions.def: 'Little' requires subject-verb inversion, showing surprise or emphasis.
questions.question: Little ___ that he was being watched.
